q: What is the primary objective of inspecting IT systems in Railway accounts?

options.B: To reduce the number of staff
options.C: To ensure data integrity, security and reliability of accounting records

q: In Railway digital accounting, what does an audit trail record?

options.B: The chronological sequence of transactions with user identity and timestamps
options.C: Only the final balance of accounts

q: Why must audit trails in accounting systems be tamper-proof?

options.D: To prevent unauthorised alteration and preserve evidence for inspection

q: What is the inspection risk if user IDs are shared among staff?

options.A: Accountability is lost and unauthorised entries cannot be traced

q: What is the accepted practice for user IDs in Railway IT applications?

options.A: No IDs needed if passwords are strong
options.B: Unique ID per user, linked to role-based access

q: What is segregation of duties in digital systems?

options.A: Splitting the office into two shifts
options.B: Dividing work so no single user can initiate, approve and complete a transaction alone

q: During inspection, what should be checked regarding password controls?

options.A: Passwords are written on desks for easy recall
options.B: All users share the admin password
options.D: Password policy enforces minimum length, complexity and periodic change

q: What does 'least privilege' mean in access control?

options.C: Access is denied to all users
options.D: Users receive only the minimum access needed for their duties

q: Why must dormant user accounts be deactivated promptly?

options.A: To reduce software licence fees only
options.C: Dormant accounts are targets for unauthorised access

q: In UTS (Unreserved Ticketing System), what is a key inspection point?

options.A: Number of fans in the booking hall
options.B: Reconciliation of ticket sales data with cash remitted to accounts

q: In PRS (Passenger Reservation System), what should inspectors verify?

options.A: That bookings, cancellations and refunds reconcile with earnings accounts

q: What does FOIS stand for in Indian Railways?
A key FOIS inspection check relates to:

options.C: Verifying freight charges billed against tariff and actual loading

q: What is data integrity in digital accounting systems?

options.B: Data is stored in large files
options.D: Data remains accurate, complete and unaltered throughout its lifecycle

q: Which control detects duplicate transactions in a system?

options.C: Unique transaction reference numbers with validation checks

q: What is an input control in a digital accounting system?

options.A: A control over the printer ink level
options.D: Checks that validate data at the point of entry, such as field formats and ranges

q: What is a processing control?

options.A: Checks that ensure transactions are processed completely and accurately by the system

q: What is an output control?

options.B: Review and reconciliation of reports generated by the system before use

q: Why is system documentation important for inspection?

options.A: It increases the weight of files
options.B: It reduces the need for computers
options.C: It makes the office look organised
options.D: It enables inspectors to understand processes, controls and data flows

q: What should inspectors check about backup procedures?

options.A: That backups are taken regularly, stored securely and restoration is tested
options.B: The name of the backup operator
options.C: The brand of the backup server

q: What is the risk of inadequate change management in IT systems?

options.B: Unauthorised or untested changes causing errors in accounting data

q: During inspection, software change logs should show:

options.A: What changed, who authorised it, when it was implemented and tested
options.C: The font used in the code

q: What is the purpose of access logs in inspection?

options.B: To count the number of computers
options.D: To review who accessed the system, when and what actions were taken

q: Why should failed login attempts be monitored?

options.B: Repeated failures may indicate a password-guessing attack

q: What is two-factor authentication?

options.A: Logging in twice with the same password
options.B: Typing the password in two languages
options.C: Verification using two independent factors, e.g. password plus one-time code

q: In digital systems, what is 'maker-checker' control?

options.B: One user creates a transaction and a different user verifies and authorises it
options.D: The printer checks the ink before printing

q: What should inspectors verify about exception reports?

options.A: They are generated, reviewed and acted upon for unusual transactions
options.B: They are stored in a locked drawer forever

q: What is a vulnerability in the context of IT inspection?

options.C: A weakness in the system that could be exploited to compromise data or operations

q: Why is timely application of security patches important?

options.A: It makes the logo look new
options.B: Patches close known vulnerabilities that attackers could exploit

q: What is the inspection concern with direct database edits bypassing the application?

options.D: They bypass application controls and audit trails, risking data manipulation

q: What does data reconciliation between systems achieve?

options.B: It confirms that figures in connected systems agree, exposing discrepancies

q: Why should master data changes be controlled?

options.B: Changes to rates, tariffs or vendor masters directly affect financial calculations

q: What is the role of supervisory review in digital transactions?

options.A: To increase the number of signatures
options.C: Independent checking of key transactions to detect errors and irregularities

q: What should an inspector check regarding year-end or period-end system procedures?

options.B: That cut-off controls correctly assign transactions to the right accounting period

q: What is 'cut-off' in accounting system terms?

options.D: The point marking which accounting period a transaction belongs to

q: Why is the physical security of servers an inspection point?

options.A: Unauthorised physical access can lead to theft, tampering or data loss

q: What is a disaster recovery plan in IT inspection context?

options.A: A plan to buy new furniture
options.C: Documented procedures to restore systems and data after a major disruption
options.D: A plan for repainting the office

q: What should inspectors verify about system-generated reports used in accounts?

options.A: They are printed on glossy paper
options.C: Report logic is tested and figures reconcile with source data

q: What is the risk of excessive privileged (admin) accounts?

options.C: More users can bypass controls and alter data without detection

q: What is log retention policy important for?

options.D: Keeping audit and access logs long enough to support inspection and investigation

q: In UTS inspection, what does 'non-issued ticket' reconciliation check?

options.A: That ticket numbers issued by the system match tickets accounted for
options.D: The colour of the ticket roll

q: What is a key PRS refund inspection check?

options.D: That refunds match cancellation records and are paid to the correct claimant

q: What does 'data migration' control ensure during system upgrades?

options.D: All data transfers completely and accurately to the new system

q: Why should test data be removed from live systems?

options.A: Test entries can distort real financial figures and mislead inspection

q: What is the purpose of periodic access reviews?

options.B: To confirm each user's access rights remain appropriate for their current role

q: What should inspectors check about interface controls between systems?

options.C: That data transfers between systems are complete, accurate and reconciled

q: What is encryption's role in protecting accounting data?

options.A: It converts data into coded form so unauthorised persons cannot read it

q: Why must cancelled or void transactions remain visible in the system?

options.C: Complete visibility preserves the audit trail and prevents concealment

q: What is a 'super user' account risk?

options.D: It has unrestricted access that can override controls and hide activity

q: What should inspection cover regarding remote access to accounting systems?

options.C: That remote access is authorised, encrypted and logged

q: What is the inspection value of trend analysis of digital transactions?

options.A: Unusual patterns can reveal errors, fraud or control failures

q: Why should system clocks be synchronised?

options.A: So the screensaver starts on time
options.D: Accurate timestamps are essential for a reliable audit trail

q: What is the purpose of a pre-implementation review of new software?

options.A: To verify controls, security and audit trails before the system goes live

q: What should inspectors verify about data archiving?

options.A: Archived data remains retrievable and readable for inspection when needed

q: What is the risk of manual workarounds bypassing system controls?

options.B: They evade automated validations and audit trails, hiding errors or fraud

q: In digital inspection, what does 'completeness' of data mean?

options.B: All transactions that should be recorded are actually recorded

q: What does 'accuracy' of data mean in system inspection?

options.D: Recorded data correctly reflects the real transaction values

q: What is the inspection significance of user activity monitoring?

options.A: It detects abnormal behaviour such as after-hours access or bulk changes
options.B: It counts mouse clicks for fun

q: Why should emergency access ('break-glass') usage be reviewed?

options.A: Emergency access bypasses normal controls and must be justified and logged

q: What is the overall assurance IT inspection provides to Railway accounts?

options.C: That digital systems produce trustworthy financial information under adequate controls
